title: Sunrise hotfix cheatsheet: quick mitigations for morning latency spikes
summary: Portable quick-reference for the morning on-call engineer to triage and apply temporary mitigations for recurring latency spikes tied to model cache cold starts and autoscaling behavior.
content:
Context:
- Seen ~3x latency spikes between 06:30-08:30 PST for the last 4 mornings. Pattern: large batch of PR-unrelated traffic, lots of new sessions, IRR increases in model KV-cache miss rate.
- Suspect: cache warmup + autoscaler slow to spin new serving replicas for peak (dedicated pools) + occasional slow kernel selection on nodes after maintenance.

Immediate triage (first 10 minutes):
1) Check pager and alert details (PagerDuty). Confirm incident scope: specific customer, region, or global.
   - pd: open top incident link, copy description to local notes.
2) Metrics quick-check (Grafana):
   - model_kv_cache_miss_rate by model and pool (look for >30% sustained)
   - pod_ready_latency, pod_restart_count, gpu_utilization by node
   - request_latency_p50/p95 by route and model
3) Infra checks (kubectl + runtime):
   - kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving --selector=app=model-server -o wide
   - kubectl describe pod <hot_pod> (look for OOM, ImagePullBackOff)
   - rwctl nodes --pool <pool-name> (shows health + available gpus)
4) Check model routing/fallbacks in console: ensure fallback model route is enabled for critical routes.

Quick mitigations (apply in order, verify impact after each):
A) Enable fallback to smaller model variant (if configured)
   - When to use: customer impact high, p95 > 10s and cache miss rate high.
   - Command: rwctl route update --route <route-id> --fallback-model <model-small>:v2
B) Scale dedicated pool temporarily (fastest visible effect)
   - Command: rwctl scale --pool morning-hotfix --replicas 6 --priority immediate
   - Note: scale ops may take 1-4 minutes depending on cloud region; prefer to scale a pool with prewarmed AMIs if available.
C) Trigger targeted prewarm for the affected model(s)
   - Script: /opt/redwood/scripts/prewarm_model_cache.sh <model-name> --concurrency 128 --prefixes-file /tmp/top-prefixes.txt
   - If missing, use a quick curl loop against model endpoint for top 50 prefixes.
D) Increase concurrent request slots on hot replicas (short-term)
   - Edit deploy config: kubectl patch deploy <model-server-deploy> -n redwood-serving --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rw/in-flight-increase":"true"}}}}}'
   - Revert after stability.
E) If GPU kernel stalls suspected, cordon and rotate a node out-of-service:
   - kubectl cordon <node> && drain --ignore-daemonsets, then restart node agent (or reboot as last resort).

Safety / Do nots (quick checklist):
- Do not restart all replicas in a pool at once. Rolling only.
- Avoid mass model rollbacks during peak unless fallback fails.
- Do not change persistent cache eviction policies without PM/SRE approval.

Notes on specific issues we've observed:
- Cache miss pattern often correlated with a purge job running at 02:00 UTC (look for cronjob model-cache-purge). If purge coincides with traffic surge, reduce purge frequency or stagger.
- Autoscaler warmup: current policy uses 6m grace period; proposal: reduce to 3m for morning windows (see linked Confluence).

Post-incident actions (capture while still hot):
- Record timeline with timestamps, commands run, metrics observed (p95 before/after).
- Create JIRA INF ticket if root cause not obvious (use INF-<next>). Attach grafana screenshots and pd logs.
- Notify product owner for affected routes and customers.

Quick commands cheat-sheet (copy-paste friendly):
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving --selector=app=model-server -o wide
- kubectl logs -n redwood-serving <pod> --since=15m | grep -Ei "error|timeout|oom"
- rwctl scale --pool morning-hotfix --replicas 6 --priority immediate
- /opt/redwood/scripts/prewarm_model_cache.sh gpt-medium --concurrency 128 --prefixes-file /tmp/top-prefixes.txt
- rwctl route update --route r-12345 --fallback-model gpt-small:v2

Unresolved / questions for follow-up:
- Which purge job is responsible for the majority of evictions? (I think cronjob/model-cache-purge on k8s-cluster-2)
- Can we add a scheduled prewarm job for the 06:00 window for top 10 models?
- Is cold-start latency quantized by kernel selection such that we can pre-select kernels during node boot?

TODOs (post-shift):
- Draft a short proposal to add a morning autoscaling profile (3m warmup, higher min replicas) for top 5 pools. @Ethan to start JIRA.
- Add a small prewarm Lambda that uses top-prefix corpus to warm caches at 05:50 local.
- Add an automated rollback guard in rwctl to prevent bad rollouts during morning window.

Personal notes (for whoever inherits this):
- If you hit a scenario where cache miss rate > 40% and p95 > 12s, prefer scaling + prewarm first before rolling back models. Rolling back often masks underlying autoscale/warmup gaps.
- Keep a slack message template handy in #sre-oncall for customer-facing updates (short, status, ETA).

References and quick links:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/model-serving
- Confluence: Model Cache Strategy (link above)
- Last related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1199
- Example incident (INF-5623) for notes format.

End of cheatsheet. Add anything you tested here so the next person has context.
